problem: Generative 3D models yield visually plausible content but not executable task environments: assets lack scale, mass, collision and simulator interfaces, and assembling them into policy-ready, navigable, editable worlds is still manual. EmbodiedGen V1 was limited to panorama-back-projected single-mesh backgrounds with little camera translation.
motivation: Closed-loop embodied policy learning (online RL, evaluation, sim-to-real) needs large numbers of physically valid, task-conditioned, portable environments. A unified sim-ready representation that keeps geometry, physics, affordances, task semantics and simulator interfaces across generation and editing would make world building scalable infrastructure.
key_idea: Build an agentic generative world engine on one sim-ready representation (assets with physics and affordances, Scene Graph task worlds, solver-based multi-room scenes, and stateful Vibe Coding editing) that exports to many simulators and supports policy training.
insight: Simulation-oriented quality gates make generated assets usable. Removing the quality checker drops human acceptance from 96.5% to 91.0%, removing mesh fixing inflates runtime about 8x (2.6 to 21.3 min) and visual mesh size (1.43 to 51.63 MB), and removing convex decomposition lowers collision success from 98.6% to 96.5%. For affordances, VLM-guided part merging raises the segmentation pass rate from 47.0% to 69.5% and end-to-end pass from 31.0% to 50.0%. Splitting the work so the LLM makes only discrete semantic decisions while deterministic solvers guarantee geometric feasibility makes edits bounded and physics-validated. The RL results come from a separate downstream study by other authors.
method: Sim-ready asset pipeline: pluggable text/image-to-3D (TRELLIS, SAM3D, Hunyuan3D) with VLM quality gates and generate-verify-retry. Mesh repair, CoACD convex decomposition, Gaussian-to-texture baking, VLM-recovered scale/mass/friction, and 3D-Fixer for occluded inputs.
Cross-simulator export: URDF as canonical form, converted to MJCF/XML (MuJoCo, Genesis) and USD (Isaac Sim), plus deformable bodies in Genesis.

Affordance autolabeling: P3-SAM part segmentation with geometric post-processing and VLM merging, GPT-5.4 part-wise semantic annotation (name, graspability, function), and GraspGen grasps validated in SAPIEN.

Task-driven interactive worlds: an LLM parses a task into a Scene Graph (robot, background, context, targets, distractors), instantiates assets online or by retrieval, and places them by BFS with support/IoU constraints and SAPIEN physics settling.

Large-scale scenes: VLM task routing (room scope, complexity tier), an Infinigen-based hierarchical constraint solver reshaped for simulation, per-instance decomposition, convex collision proxies and centroid canonicalization, exported as URDF/USD.

Stateful Vibe Coding: an agent-skill-harness where an LLM agent Parse/Ground/Invoke/Commit loop calls deterministic skills (asset-creator, room-creator, layout-creator, spatial-computing, sim-runner) over a persistent world state (Scene Graph, assets, poses, history).
Downstream validation: generated scenes used by other authors for online RL of a pi0-style VLA and sim-to-real transfer.

setting.backbone: Pluggable frozen generative models (SAM3D used for evaluation; TRELLIS, Hunyuan3D), LLM/VLM agents (GPT-5.4 for affordance annotation; Codex/Gemini CLI for Vibe Coding); downstream VLA is a pi0-style policy fine-tuned with RL (by a separate study)
setting.training_data: none (pipeline of pretrained models and deterministic solvers); the downstream RL study uses a pi0-style policy pretrained on BridgeV2 and fine-tuned online in generated scenes
setting.observation: not applicable to the generation pipeline (image or text inputs); downstream VLA uses RGB manipulation observations
setting.action_space: not applicable to the generation pipeline; downstream VLA does robot manipulation actions
setting.simulator: SAPIEN (validation), Genesis, MuJoCo, Isaac Sim/Gym, PyBullet via RoboVerse

numbers_note: No embodied navigation benchmark results. The paper reports generation-quality metrics and summarized downstream manipulation RL results (9.7% to 79.8% sim success, 21.7% to 75.0% real success), which are not on any listed benchmark.
results: The asset pipeline reaches 96.5% human acceptance and 98.6% collision success at 2.6 min per asset. 83.3% of 150 task-driven worlds are usable without manual modification, at 47.7 min per world with online generation. In the cited downstream study, online RL in generated scenes raises simulation success from 9.7% to 79.8% and real-robot success from 21.7% to 75.0%, and a policy trained on three hand-built SimplerEnv scenes reaches only 36.0% on generated scenes.
limitations: Online world generation is slow (47.7 min per world, 25.5 min per background), and about 17% of worlds fail from scale mismatch, geometry defects or unstable placement.
Affordance end-to-end yield is only 50.0%, and the RL and sim-to-real evidence comes from a separate study by other authors, not tested in this paper.
Large-scale multi-room scenes, navigation and Vibe Coding are shown qualitatively, with no quantitative navigation or editing evaluation.
